A cross-product component proves curvature can vanish only when \(\sin(qt)=0\); the remaining components identify \(R=1+x\), \(\cos(qt)=-1\). Strict convexity of \(F\), its negative central value, and both endpoint factors prove exactly one simple root in each permitted half-interval. Interior roots lift to \(2q\) parameter points, the outer endpoint to \(q\) double torsion zeros, while the inner endpoint consists of excluded zero-curvature points. SymPy identities, independent Cartesian numerical determinants and sample root counts successfully replay.
